_meta.project: instex Instrument Explorer -- IMAGER preset: 2MASS (two identical 1.3 m Cassegrain telescopes, Mt. Hopkins and CTIO, each with a three-channel J/H/Ks NICMOS3 camera; freeze-frame scanning survey)
_meta.companion: data/imaging/twomass.md (same content as Markdown). Structure follows data/imaging/widefield.json / tess.json: sources{key: cite, file, url}; twomass: title, preset (machine-readable explorer inputs), preset_alt_coldstop, recommended_preset (prose), params (telescope, camera, detector), survey (freeze-frame scanning), performance (validation targets), not_found, conflicts, notes (+ notes_quotes).
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from a document saved unmodified under rawdata/imaging/2mass/. DERIVED = arithmetic done here (shown). alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). Every quote except those from sources or entries with check = "image" was machine-checked against the saved file's extracted text: pdftotext -layout and -raw per page, tag-stripped HTML and raw HTML source (null padding removed, Latin-1), the ADS JSON record raw and field by field.
_meta.quote_normalisation: Unicode NFKC; curly quotes, dashes, minus, primes and the acute accent used as an arcsec mark (U+00B4) normalised; NUL bytes removed; in the S06 text layer the control character used for mu restored as mu and those used for superscript minus, sigma and tilde dropped; whitespace collapsed (a quote also passes if it matches with all whitespace removed, which covers HTML <sub> splits such as "K s"); " ... " joins non-adjacent pieces of the same page or file.
_meta.frames: One 256 x 256 array per band; x = rows of the array. On the sky the arrays are rotated ~0.2-0.4 deg from north-south (columns ~along declination, the scan direction).

S06.cite: Skrutskie, M. F., Cutri, R. M., Stiening, R., Weinberg, M. D., Schneider, S., Carpenter, J. M., et al. 2006, AJ 131, 1163, "The Two Micron All Sky Survey (2MASS)" (publisher PDF, 21 pp.; journal pages 1163-1183 = PDF pp. 1-21). Table 1 = survey parameters; Sec. 2.2 arrays, cameras and bandpasses; Sec. 2.3 telescopes; Sec. 2.4 site conditions; Sec. 3.2 image acquisition; Sec. 3.3 tiling; Sec. 4.3 Atlas Images. Its text layer renders the arcsec glyph as "B" after a digit (2B0 = 2.0"), as "00" after an integer (5700 = 57", 100 = 1", 8300 = 83", 1000 = 10", 5000 = 50"), the arcmin glyph as "A" (8A5 = 8.5'), the degree glyph as "N" (0N3 = 0.3 deg), "x" as ";" and "=" as "1/4" (the single glyph U+00BC); the superscript minus, sigma, mu and tilde are control characters (mu restored, the others dropped in the normalised text)

twomass.title: 2MASS: two identical 1.3 m classical Cassegrain telescopes (Mt. Hopkins, CTIO), each with a cryogenic three-channel reimaging camera (J, H, Ks at once through two dichroics; one 256 x 256 NICMOS3 per band, 40 um = 2.0"); freeze-frame scanning survey

preset.telescope_type: classical Cassegrain (paraboloidal primary f/2.0, hyperboloidal secondary), 1.3 m, open tube, equatorial fork; the secondary tilts in declination for freeze-frame scanning; two identical telescopes (Mt. Hopkins, Arizona; Cerro Tololo, Chile)
preset.D_note: primary mirror 1300 mm (1280 mm clear, GM20); the camera's cold Lyot stops pass 90% of the pupil diameter (1.17 m equivalent, DERIVED; see preset_alt_coldstop)
preset.eps_note: 232-mm secondary / 1300-mm primary (DERIVED; 228/1280 = 0.178 from GM20); no baffles during 2MASS; the 200-mm primary hole lies inside the secondary shadow
preset.F_note: f_eff / 1.3 m from the published Cassegrain plate scale 11.97"/mm (DERIVED); published label f/13.5
preset.back_note: native Cassegrain focus 527 mm behind the primary vertex (GM20); drawing only
preset.field_note: no telescope corrected field is published; 12.1' just encloses the 8.49' square array (diagonal 12.01'); a cryogenic field stop at the Cassegrain focus is slightly smaller than the array image
preset.imager: reimaged (cryogenic, all-refractive, all-spherical; 1 common collimating lens + 2 dichroics + 6 lenses per band; Lyot stop and filter at a pupil image in each band)
preset.W_note: NOT FOUND (pupil / Lyot-stop diameter is in Milligan et al. 1996, not obtained); the pixel scale and field do not depend on W
preset.Fc_note: f_eff / 1.3 m with f_eff = 40 um x 206264.8 / 1.991" = 4144 mm (DERIVED); design F/3.5 (M96) is the 90%-cold-stopped beam (4144 / 1170 = 3.54)
preset.cold_stop: Lyot stop diameter = 90% of the pupil image (S06)
preset.bands_simultaneous: J, H, Ks imaged at once through two dichroics (J reflected first, H reflected second, Ks straight through)
preset.n_chips_note: one NICMOS3 per band, three per camera, co-aligned (not a mosaic)
preset.detector: Rockwell NICMOS3 HgCdTe, 256 x 256, 40 um, four 128 x 128 quadrants
preset.seeing_note: S06 Sec. 2.1: a typical seeing disc is 1" FWHM; the measured frame FWHM of 2.5-2.8" includes the 2" pixels

survey.technique: freeze-frame scanning: continuous declination scan at 57"/s; the secondary tilts against the scan (sawtooth) to hold the image still for each 1.3 s exposure, then flies back during readout/reset
survey.tile: 504" (RA) x (6 deg + 8.5') (Dec); 273 (N) / 274 (S) frames; ~7 min per scan; 59,650 tiles

pub_suggested.src: Skrutskie+06; circular: F_cam was derived from it
no published value; 0.0207 with the 1.17 m cold stop

preset.pub_unmodelled: design final focal ratio F/3.5 (Milligan+96; the model gives 3.19 with D = 1.3 m, 3.54 with D = 1.17 m); Cassegrain plate scale 11.97″/mm (Skrutskie+06; circular, F was derived from it)
preset.flags: F DERIVED from the published plate scale (label f/13.5); F_cam DERIVED from the pixel scale (design F/3.5 refers to the cold-stopped beam); eps DERIVED from the secondary diameter; W, f_col, f_cam NOT FOUND (only their ratio); field circle chosen to enclose the array

preset_alt_coldstop.purpose: variant with the aperture set by the cold Lyot stop (90% of the pupil diameter); same pixel scale and field
preset_alt_coldstop.basis: DERIVED: D = 0.9 x 1.3 m; eps = 0.232 / 1.17 (assumes the stop does not also mask the centre: not published); F = 17,232 / 1170; Fc = 4144 / 1170 (matches the design F/3.5 of M96)

twomass.recommended_preset: Classical Cassegrain, reimaged. D = 1.3 m (primary; 1280 mm clear), eps = 0.178 (232-mm secondary / 1300 mm, DERIVED; no baffles during 2MASS), F = 13.26 DERIVED from the published Cassegrain plate scale 11.97"/mm (f_eff = 17,232 mm; published label f/13.5), primary f/2.0 (R = 5200 mm, paraboloid; drawing only), Cassegrain focus 527 mm behind the primary vertex (back = 0.405 D). Camera: LN2 cryostat behind a ZnSe window; a cryogenic field stop at the Cassegrain focus, one common Infrasil collimating lens, two dichroics in the nearly collimated beam (J reflected first, H reflected by the second, Ks straight through), then six lenses per band forming a pupil image with a cold Lyot stop of 90% of the pupil diameter and the band filter beside it; all 19 lenses spherical CaF2/Infrasil, design F/3.5. W (pupil diameter) NOT FOUND; F_cam = 3.188 DERIVED from 40 um at 1.991"/px (f_eff = 4144 mm; f_cam/f_col = 0.2405). Detector per band: one Rockwell NICMOS3 HgCdTe 256 x 256, 40 um; three co-aligned arrays per camera, rows [1], no gaps. Field 8.5 x 8.5 arcmin (circle 12.1' encloses it). Survey: freeze-frame scanning at 57"/s in declination, secondary sawtooth holds each 1.3 s exposure (1.455 s cycle), step 82.6" (N) / 82.3" (S), six frames per point = 7.8 s; tiles 504" x (6 deg + 8.5'), 273/274 frames; Atlas Images resampled to 1"/px (512 x 1024 px) from the 2" raw pixels. Validate: 1.991"/px (1.980-2.006 by array), 8.5' field, 10-sigma limits J/H/Ks 15.8/15.1/14.3 required, 16.42/15.48/14.81 mean achieved, image FWHM 2.5-2.8". Band: Ks (J and H identical optics; plate scales within 1%).

telescope_aperture.quote: 2MASS used two custom 1.3 m equatorial telescopes.
telescope_aperture.note: The camera's cold Lyot stops are 90% of the pupil diameter (S06 Sec. 2.2, under cold_stop below), so the beam that reaches the detectors comes from the central 0.9 x 1.3 = 1.17 m of the primary (DERIVED, assuming the pupil image is the 1.3 m primary). The explorer preset keeps D = 1.3 m; the cold-stop variant is given as preset_alt_coldstop.

alternatives.quote: The 2MASS project was carried out with two identical 1.3-meter aperture, open-tube, equatorial fork-mount telescopes.
Primary Mirror: 1300 mm diameter, radius of curvature 5200 mm, conic constant -1.000
The parabolic primary mirror has a radius of curvature of R = 5200 mm, and a clear diameter of D1,clear = 1280 mm.
alternatives.note: clear aperture of the northern telescope (Tierras refurbishment)

alternatives.quote: 1.3 m equatorial Cassegrain

telescope_aperture.derived: DERIVED: cold-stop-limited aperture 0.9 x 1300 = 1170 mm (0.9 x 1280 = 1152 mm on the GM20 clear aperture).

central_obstruction.unit: linear ratio (DERIVED: secondary diameter / primary diameter)
central_obstruction.quote: Secondary Mirror: 232 mm diameter, radius of curvature 965.7 mm, conic constant -1.847
central_obstruction.note: What sets eps: the secondary mirror. The telescope carried no light baffles during 2MASS (GM20 Sec. 6.1), and the 200-mm primary hole (GM20) lies inside the secondary's shadow (200/1300 = 0.154). The size of the secondary cell and of its tilt (freeze-frame) mechanism is not published. Whether the cold Lyot stop also masks the centre is not published; if it trims only the outer edge, eps relative to the 1.17 m stopped beam is 232/1170 = 0.198 (DERIVED).

alternatives.value: 228 mm secondary clear / 1280 mm primary clear
alternatives.quote: The hyperbolic (K = -1.847) secondary mirror has R = 965.7 mm, and D2,clear = 228 mm.
the 1.3-m telescope was not equipped with light baffles while the 2MASS and PAIRITEL projects were carried out
Aiming for a larger FOV was impractical due to vignetting at the primary mirror hole (Dhole = 200 mm).

central_obstruction.derived: DERIVED: 232 / 1300 = 0.1785; 228 / 1280 = 0.1781; primary hole 200 / 1300 = 0.154 (smaller, so not the limit); 232 / 1170 = 0.198 against the cold-stopped beam.

telescope_focus.value: classical Cassegrain (paraboloidal primary, hyperboloidal secondary), open tube, equatorial fork mount; the secondary is articulated in declination for freeze-frame scanning
telescope_focus.quote: For each telescope, the primary mirror, composed of Corning ultra-low expansion glass, is parabolic with a radius of curvature of 5200 mm. The secondary conic constant is 1.847 with a radius of curvature of 965.7 mm.
telescope_focus.note: Not a Ritchey-Chretien: an RC has a hyperboloidal primary, while the 2MASS primary has conic constant -1.000 (a paraboloid). In the S06 text layer the minus sign of the secondary conic is a control character (dropped from the normalised quote); ES-III.1a and GM20 print -1.847. Paraxial check (DERIVED from the published radii): with the focus 527 mm behind the primary vertex (GM20) the secondary magnification is 6.627, f = 6.627 x 2600 mm = 17,230 mm, plate scale 11.971"/mm, matching S06's 11.97"/mm; the classical-Cassegrain condition K2 = -((m+1)/(m-1))^2 = -1.847 holds at m = 6.570 (back focus 499 mm).

alternatives.quote: These telescopes have been provided with a Cassegrain focus mount for the infrared cameras and a secondary mirror, which is articulated in the declination direction.
Primary Mirror: 1300 mm diameter, radius of curvature 5200 mm, conic constant -1.000
1.3 m equatorial Cassegrain

focal_ratio.unit: f/# at the Cassegrain focus (DERIVED: f_eff / 1.3 m from the published plate scale; published f/13.5)
focal_ratio.quote: These optics provide a Cassegrain focal ratio of f/13.5 and a Cassegrain plate scale of 11B97 mm
focal_ratio.note: The two published numbers disagree by 1.8%: f/13.5 x 1.3 m = 17,550 mm would give 11.75"/mm. The paraxial prescription at the 527-mm back focus gives 11.971"/mm (telescope_focus), so the plate scale is the consistent number and f/13.5 a rounded label. The model's final pixel scale does not depend on F (only on F_cam x D).

alternatives.quote: A cryogenic field stop lies at the f /13.5 telescope Cassegrain focal plane directly behind the dewar window.
They provide a Cassegrain focal ratio of f /13.5 and a plate scale of 11.9400 mm
alternatives.note: GM20 text layer: "11.9400 mm-1" = 11.94" mm^-1; 11.94"/mm gives f = 17,275 mm, f/13.29 (DERIVED)

effective_focal_length_cassegrain.unit: mm (DERIVED from the 11.97"/mm Cassegrain plate scale)

alternatives.quote: a plate scale of 11.9400 mm
Cassegrain focal ratio of f/13.5

primary_focal_ratio.unit: f/# of the primary (DERIVED; drawing only)
primary_focal_ratio.quote: Primary Mirror: 1300 mm diameter, radius of curvature 5200 mm
primary_focal_ratio.derived: DERIVED: f1 = R/2 = 2600 mm; 2600 / 1300 = f/2.00. Secondary: R = 965.7 mm, f2 = -482.85 mm (convex); at the 527-mm back focus it sits 2190 mm in front of the primary, 410 mm inside the prime focus, where the axial beam is 205 mm wide (DERIVED, paraxial; the 232-mm secondary is 13% larger).

cassegrain_focus_position.unit: mm behind the primary vertex (northern telescope, native focal plane; back/D = 0.405 DERIVED)
cassegrain_focus_position.quote: at the native focal plane, located 527 mm behind the primary vertex

alternatives.value: field stop 10 cm behind the dewar window
alternatives.quote: Light enters through the ZnSe window at right. The Cassegrain focal plane lies 10 cm behind the window at a cryogenic field stop.

cassegrain_focus_position.derived: DERIVED: 527 / 1300 = 0.405 D. The 2MASS camera position during the survey is not published separately.

field.value: 8.5 x 8.5 (set by the arrays; the cryogenic field stop at the Cassegrain focus is slightly undersized relative to the array images)
field.quote: The field stop, located at the overlapping conjugate images of the arrays themselves, is slightly undersized relative to the array images in order to prevent light from scattering from the rough edge of the sapphire array substrate.
field.note: No corrected or unvignetted telescope field is published for 2MASS. GM20 (Sec. 2), designing a focal reducer for the same telescope, found a field larger than about 0.5 deg impractical because of vignetting at the 200-mm primary hole. For the explorer's circular field use 12.1' (just encloses the 8.50' square array, diagonal 12.01' DERIVED).
field.derived: DERIVED: 256 px x 1.991"/px = 509.7" = 8.49'; diagonal 720.8" = 12.01'. At the Cassegrain focus the array image is 509.7" / 11.97"/mm = 42.6 mm square (the field-stop size, approximately).

imager.value: reimaged, all refractive and cryogenic: field stop at the Cassegrain focus, one common collimating lens, two dichroics in the nearly collimated beam, then per band six lenses that form a pupil image (cold Lyot stop + filter) and reimage the sky on the array
imager.quote: The low irradiance of astronomical sources, combined with background limited performance of the detectors, mandated a reimaging configuration and the enclosure of the camera optics within the cold volume.

alternatives.value: one common lens + six lenses per band
alternatives.quote: The first Infrasil lens, common to all bands, relays nearly collimated light to beamsplitting mirrors. Following the beam splitters, the light for each band encounters independent identical sets of six lenses, which relay images of the sky onto the three arrays.
path to each array traverses seven lenses.
The final F/3.5 optical design uses fifteen CaF<SUB>2</SUB> elements and four Infrasil elements in an all-spherical configuration.
alternatives.note: 1 common + 3 x 6 = 19 lenses (DERIVED), consistent with S06

alternatives.value: all lenses spherical, Infrasil or CaF2
alternatives.quote: The lenses were composed of water-free fused silica (Infrasil) or calcium fluoride. All lens surfaces were spherical.
A liquid nitrogen cryostat encloses all of the 2MASS optical elements and arrays with the exception of the ZnSe dewar entrance window.

collimator.quote: The first Infrasil lens, common to all bands, relays nearly collimated light to beamsplitting mirrors.
collimator.note: The collimator is the single Infrasil lens just behind the field stop, shared by the three bands. Its focal length and the beam diameter are in Milligan et al. (1996), which was not obtained. In the model f_col = F x W.

cold_stop.value: Lyot stop at a pupil image in each band, diameter 90% of the pupil image (pupil diameter W NOT FOUND)
cold_stop.quote: These calcium fluoride and Infrasil lenses form pupil images at three Lyot stops adjacent to the band-limiting interference filters. The stop diameter is 90% of the pupil diameter to permit some freedom for misalignment of the three stops relative to one another.
cold_stop.note: The pupil (Lyot-stop) diameter in mm is not in any source obtained (Milligan et al. 1996 has the prescription). The model's pixel scale and field do not depend on W (f_col = F W, f_cam = F_cam W).

camera_focal_ratio.unit: F_cam = f_eff / D (DERIVED from the mean pixel scale with D = 1.3 m; design F/3.5 for the cold-stopped beam)
camera_focal_ratio.quote: The average plate scale for all six arrays (three northern and three southern) was 1B991 pixel
camera_focal_ratio.note: F/3.5 (M96) is the design focal ratio of the beam at the detector. With the full 1.3 m aperture the published pixel scale implies f/3.19; with the 90% cold stop (1.17 m) it implies f/3.54, i.e. the design F/3.5 refers to the stopped beam (DERIVED consistency check).

alternatives.quote: The final F/3.5 optical design uses fifteen CaF<SUB>2</SUB> elements
When mounted on the 2MASS telescopes ( Figure 7 ) each pixel subtended approximately 2.0" on the sky.

image_quality_optics.value: ~90% of a laboratory point source's energy within one 40 um pixel; diffraction limited over the format at Ks, nearly so at J and H (design)
image_quality_optics.quote: For a laboratory point source, the optics concentrated approximately 90% of the image's energy onto a square area defined by one 40 micron NICMOS3 pixel.

alternatives.quote: The design is diffraction limited over the full format in the Ks spectral band, and is nearly so in the J and H bands.

dichroic_split.value: J reflected by the first ("J") dichroic; H transmitted by it and reflected by the second ("H") dichroic; Ks transmitted by both (straight through)
dichroic_split.quote: J-band experiences only a reflection off of the "J-band dichroic." H-band must traverse the J-band dichroic and then experience a reflection off of the "H-band dichroic." Ks band traverses both dichroics.

alternatives.quote: Two dichroic mirrors immediately follow this common lens to split the light between the three bandpasses with the J-band light reflected first and the Ks-band light undeviated.
In Figure 1, the straight-through light path leads to the K s array, the upper path to the J array, and the lower one to H.
ray trace: one shared front group, a fold to each of two side channels, one straight-through channel; three array housings

alternatives.value: all three arrays view the same sky

Optics transmission: "~70%" for the integrated optical assembly (ES-III.1b) vs "over 80%" for all lenses combined (ES-III.1b1; lenses only, so not necessarily a conflict).
notes: Telescope model: Cassegrain, D = 1.3 m, eps = 0.178, F = 13.26 (published f/13.5), primary f/2.0; the explorer's "cass" type. The real primary is a paraboloid, the secondary a hyperboloid (K = -1.847): a classical Cassegrain, not a Ritchey-Chretien.

Camera model: reimaged with an ideal collimator f_col = F W and camera f_cam = F_cam W, F_cam = 3.188. The real camera is a dioptric relay: field stop at the Cassegrain focus, one common lens that nearly collimates the beam, two dichroic beam splitters in that beam, then an identical six-lens group per band that forms a pupil image (Lyot stop + interference filter) and reimages the sky onto a NICMOS3 array. Only the reduction f_cam/f_col = 0.2405 is fixed by the published plate scales.

Bands: the three channels are optically identical and see the same sky (common centre within 10"); per-array plate scales differ by < 1% (1.980-2.006"/px). One preset serves J, H and Ks; switching band changes only lambda.

Cold stop: the Lyot stops are 90% of the pupil diameter, so the effective light-collecting aperture is 1.17 m (DERIVED); the design F/3.5 matches this stopped beam. preset_alt_coldstop gives the variant D = 1.17 m, eps = 0.198, F = 14.73, F_cam = 3.542.

Freeze-frame scanning: instead of stepping and settling, the whole telescope scans steadily north-south at 57"/s while the secondary mirror tilts the other way so the image stands still on the arrays for each 1.3 s exposure; then the secondary snaps back (< 0.1 s, during reset/readout) and the next frame starts 82.6" further along, just under 1/6 of the 8.5' frame. Every point is therefore seen six times (7.8 s), at six different sub-pixel positions (non-integer step + ~0.3 deg array rotation), which the pipeline exploits to build Atlas Images on a 1" grid from 2" pixels.
Sampling: the raw 2" pixels undersample even 1" seeing; measured frame FWHM is 2.5-2.8". The Atlas Images (1" pixels) are a kernel-smoothed coadd, not a higher-resolution optical image.
